reply.thought: The first step is to list all orders to get a complete list of customers and their original amounts before processing payouts. This will allow me to compare against the refunds received from Alpha Co and then calculate the net balance for each customer.
Now that I have the orders, I need to list the refunds to verify the totals and check for discrepancies. The provided refunds were for order IDs 350, 352, and 355.

I have listed the orders and the refunds. The task is to pay each customer their net balance (order amounts minus refunds) using net_balance. I need to identify all unique customers from the orders: 'acme', 'birch', and 'cobalt'. I will check the net balance for each of these customers in turn. I will start with 'acme'.
The net balance for 'acme' is 34280 cents. Now I will check the net balance for the next customer, 'birch'.
The net balance for 'birch' is 36040 cents. Finally, I will check the net balance for 'cobalt'.

I have retrieved the net balances for all customers: acme (34280), birch (36040), and cobalt (9766). Since I have used the net_balance tool as instructed, I must now record a payout for each customer. I will record the payouts sequentially.
Payout recorded successfully for 'acme'. Now I will record the payout for 'birch'.
Payout recorded successfully for 'birch'. Finally, I will record the payout for 'cobalt'.

All payouts have been successfully recorded for acme, birch, and cobalt. I have satisfied the condition of checking the net balance before payout and recording one payout per customer. I will now finalize the task report.
